recipes.name: Winter Fruit Salad with Poppyseed Dressing
ingredients_raw: 1 head romaine lettuce, torn into bite-size pieces

steps.text: Combine sugar, lemon juice, onion, mustard, and salt in a food processor or blender; process until well blended. With machine still running, add oil in a slow, steady stream until mixture is thick and smooth. Add poppy seeds, and process just a few seconds more to mix.
Toss romaine lettuce, shredded Swiss cheese, cashews, dried cranberries, apple, and pear together in a large serving bowl. Pour dressing over salad just before serving, and toss to coat.

raw_recipe.headline: Winter Fruit Salad with Poppyseed Dressing
raw_recipe.description: A wonderful winter fruit salad with apple, pear, cranberries, cashews, and shredded Swiss cheese tossed in a sweet-tangy lemon and poppyseed dressing.

review.reviewBody:
I don't give out 5 star ratings as often as I used to but we really enjoyed this salad and it is a definite keeper. I made a few small changes: chopped green leaf lettuce instead of romaine, roasted pecans instead of cashews, at least twice as much apple and pear and about 2 TBS less sugar. I wanted to have everything ready about an hour before it was time to toss everything together so I tossed the sliced apples and pears with some of the dressing. Besides staying nice and white they absorbed some of the wonderful dressing flavor. We enjoyed the Swiss cheese, but I want to try this with blue cheese next time. I think the sweetness of the dressing and the saltiness of the blue cheese would be perfect. 12/2004
Update 9/2007: I finally made this using blue cheese and I love it! My husband and I both liked it much better than the swiss cheese and this is the only way I will make it from now on.

I made this at the last moment with ingredients I had on hand, but it was awesome! The lemon dressing I had made the night before was awful and I had company coming so I had to improvise. I found this recipe and made a few changes. I didn't have an onion but the dressing needed something so I substitued minced ginger-wow! This was amazing! I also kept my greens, crunchies, fruit and dressing separate so my guests could add what they wanted. Six people finished the whole salad. I used 1/3 cup walnuts, 1/3 cup almonds and 2 T flax seed-toasted-for my crunchies. The fruit I had on hand was 2 clementines, 2 granny smiths and 1/4 cup dried cranberries. My salad greens included 5 oz. of baby lettuces and half a package of spinach. Can't wait to make this again-thanks!

Made it for thanksgiving but used bottled dressing to save time. We loved it. Directions called for peeling the fruits, which I did, but the picture shows the skins still on. I will leave the skins on next time for the extra color and to save even more time. I made it earlier in the day so to keep the fruit from turning brown, I tossed a small amount of the dressing to coat the fruit. Most people did not want extra dressing when it was served.

This salad is fabulous! I made it for Christmas and it was a huge hit. I used two romaine hearts and a small bag of mixed baby greens. I made the dressing the day before to let the flavors meld. Before serving it, I blended it together with a hand blender which emulsified it. Before I added the apple and pear pieces to the salad or dressed the salad, I dredged them in the dressing. Then added the fruit and nuts and tossed it all with the dressing. The recipe made more dressing than we needed but we used it with other greens the next day. Thanks very much or such a wonderful recipe!!

Definitely way way way too much dressing! Cut in 1/2 if not 1/3 and then just drizzle small amounts at a time and toss to coat. A little big goes a long way - just a light coating. Just make sure you wait to put on the dressing until ready to serve, otherwise lettuce gets soggy. 

Used red leaf lettuce the 2nd time which was just as good if not better. I used 2 apples which may be why I didn't miss the crunch of the romaine.

I now make this salad with pecans and omit the cheese.

This recipe is very yummy! 
I gave this a three star rating because I changed it a bit as follows:

1/4 cup sugar
1 tablespoon dijon
1/3 cup veg. oil

Everything else I kept the same. I felt that there was way to much sugar, and oil. With fiddling with the amounts I found it can increase the actual taste over sweetness. 
Increasing the Dijon mustard, and decreasing the sugar brings out the lemon, and Dijon tangy-ness that creates a more subtle taste.

I made this as part of our Christmas dinner and was a huge hit! I do have to admit to speed things up in my hectic cooking schedule I used pre-made poppy seed dressing and bagged already chopped romaine! Used all the other ingredients though! Thank you!

so delicious. I used a granny smith apple but i have used a macintosh in the past and both are great in this salad. Usually I keep the salad dressing the same as the recipe, which is delicious, but this time I switched maple syrup 1:1 for the sugar and added a cup of strawberries to blend in the blender for the dressing and it was splendid. Great salad as is, great with a few twists too!

I made 1/2 the recipe and decreased the sugar just a tad. I tasted it, and adjusted the dressing to suit my family's taste. We prefer a less sweet dressing. I added about 2 tablespoons of red wine vinegar, a little freshly ground black pepper and a pinch more of salt and two tablespoons of oil. Overall, a delicious dressing for the broccoli, kale, cabbage, cranberry and pumpkin seed salad we like to make. Thank you!

Very refreshing and delicious. I had dried sour cherries on hand, so used those instead of dried cranberries. I also changed up the dressing a bit, using a couple of TBSP of honey instead of sugar, half lemon juice and half flavoured balsamic vinegar and omitting the mustard and onion.

The ladies loved it! I makes a lot and you will want to use it again and again. It will work with many fruit and cheese combinations. I used raspberries, apples, pears and the dried cranberries w/ blue cheese on a crunchy green leaf. Lovely.

Served to a large crowd who all raved about it. Substituted raspberry poppy seed dressing from the store to save time. The flavors blended into surprisingly delicious combos — considering how easily it came together. I salted and roasted the cashews and used blue cheese crumbles. Thanks for the great recipe.
I made this recipe as written and it was a hit. Oh, except that I used feta as that was what I had on hand. I will certainly be making this again.

A Holiday Staple! A co-worker brought this to a pot luck several years ago and I've been making it every year at Christmastime since. I just love it and so does everyone who tastes it. Wouldn't be Christmas for me without it!

I paired this salad with a savory ham and cheese bread pudding for brunch and the combination was so tasty. I subsituted pickled red onions in the dressing and mixed nuts instead of just cashews. Delicious and easy to make!
Still one of my go to holiday recipes love love love
My first review was several year ago this continues to be a favorite! I do cut down on the sugar by about 1/4th. I've used oranges, apples, pears, mango and permanganates all are excellent!
I absolutely love this! My fav salad! Always at hit at parties & gatherings! Thank you!
